title: Cone triangles in the localization of finite filtered complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let $\mathcal C$ be the additive category of finite decreasingly filtered objects with filtration-preserving maps [def-sp-filtration], or its full additive subcategory specified by fixed integers $a\le b$ and the bounds $F^aX=X$, $F^{b+1}X=0$. Let $K^+(\mathcal C)$ be the category of bounded-below integer-indexed cochain complexes modulo filtration-preserving chain homotopies. A complex is graded acyclic if all its graded complexes [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] have zero cohomology [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $W$ consist of maps inducing quasi-isomorphisms on every graded complex. The category $K^+(\mathcal C)$ is triangulated [def-weil-triangulated-category], with shifts and cone triangles given by the cochain formulas in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the direct-sum filtration on cones. For every full additive subcategory $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal C$, the category $K^+(\mathcal J)$ has the same cone triangulation and its inclusion into $K^+(\mathcal C)$ is exact. A map lies in $W$ if and only if its cone is graded acyclic. The localization $Q:K^+(\mathcal C)\to K^+(\mathcal C)[W^{-1}]$ is a triangulated category with distinguished triangles the triangles isomorphic to images of cone triangles, and $Q$ is exact. Localizations and morphisms are taken in a universe large enough to contain them.

source.place: Tag 05RX (section-filtered-derived-category), the paragraph on additive exact functors from homotopy categories; Tag 05S1 (lemma-filtered-acyclic), Tag 05S2 (definition-filtered-derived). Apply the same cone-localization construction to bounded-below complexes and, separately, to the additive category with a fixed filtration interval.

proof.text: Finite filtered objects form an additive category: use the zero object and biproducts of $\mathcal A$, with $F^p(X\oplus Y)=F^pX\oplus F^pY$ [def-sp-filtration]. Composition is bilinear on the subgroups of filtration-preserving maps. Finite sums of finite filtrations remain finite; if bounds $[a,b]$ are prescribed, they remain $F^a=X\oplus Y$ and $F^{b+1}=0$. Apply [lem-trf-additive-homotopy-category-triangulated] to this additive category $\mathcal C$. It gives the unbounded homotopy category $K(\mathcal C)$ its cochain shift and direct-sum cone triangulation.

source.place: Tag 014S (proposition-homotopy-category-triangulated); Tag 05RX (section-filtered-derived-category), finite filtered objects are additive

proof.text: Pass to bounded-below complexes using [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. They form a full additive subcategory of $K(\mathcal C)$: a homotopy between two such complexes has the same components and equations in either category. Zero and both shifts are bounded below. If $X^n=0$ for $n<N_X$ and $Y^n=0$ for $n<N_Y$, then $C(f)^n=Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}=0$ for $n<\min(N_Y,N_X-1)$. For a distinguished triangle $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$ whose outer vertices are bounded below, rotate to $Z[-1]\to X\to Y\to Z$; TR3 with identity maps on the first two vertices gives a triangle morphism from the cone triangle of $Z[-1]\to X$, and [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes its third component an isomorphism. This cone is bounded below. Thus the inherited triangulation exists, its triangles are precisely those isomorphic inside this subcategory to its cone triangles, and its inclusion is exact. This is $K^+(\mathcal C)$.

For every filtration index $p$, taking $\operatorname{gr}^p$ commutes with the finite direct sums in a cone and with the shift, and the quotient formula identifies $\operatorname{gr}^p(\operatorname{Cone}(f))$ with the ordinary mapping cone of $\operatorname{gr}^p(f)$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. By [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic], $\operatorname{gr}^p(f)$ is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when this graded cone is acyclic. Hence $f\in W$ exactly when every graded piece of its cone is acyclic, which is the asserted filtered-acyclic cone criterion.

source.place: Tag 05S1, definition-filtered-acyclic and lemma-filtered-acyclic; Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic

proof.text: Let $\mathcal S$ be the full subcategory of $K^+(\mathcal C)$ consisting of graded-acyclic complexes. The graded functors preserve homotopies (apply their additive maps to $f-g=dh+hd$), so cohomology of each grade is well-defined and sends isomorphisms to isomorphisms; hence $\mathcal S$ is replete. Zero and shifts belong to $\mathcal S$. If $X,Y\in\mathcal S$, every $H^n(\operatorname{gr}^p f)$ is the isomorphism $0\to0$; Step 3 and [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] show $C(f)\in\mathcal S$. In a triangle with outer vertices in $\mathcal S$, rotate once backwards; TR3 and [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso], applied with identity maps on its first two vertices, identify its third vertex with the cone between those shifted outer vertices. Hence the original middle vertex belongs to $\mathcal S$. Thus [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory] makes $\mathcal S$ a full replete triangulated subcategory. This verifies the needed kernel closure directly.

source.place: Tag 05S1 (lemma-filtered-acyclic), its triangulated-kernel closure, using the cone criterion of Tag 05RT (lemma-acyclic)

proof.text: By Step 3, a map lies in $W$ exactly when its cone belongs to $\mathcal S$. Apply the existing Mathlib leaf [lem-trf-triangulated-subcategory-cone-system] to $K^+(\mathcal C)$ and $\mathcal S$ from Step 4. Its conclusion supplies identities and composition, both left and right calculi of fractions (both Ore and both cancellation axioms), shift invariance, and completion of a commuting square between distinguished triangles whose first two vertical maps lie in $W$ by a third map in $W$. These are exactly the multiplicative-system and triangulation-compatibility hypotheses [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization].

source.place: Tag 05RG (lemma-construct-multiplicative-system), first assertion; applied as in Tag 05S1 (lemma-filtered-acyclic)

proof.text: Localize $K^+(\mathcal C)$ at the multiplicative system $W$ of Step 5, with the universal property in [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization]. Apply [lem-pur-localization-triangles-05r6] to this triangulated category and compatible system. It gives the triangulation of $K^+(\mathcal C)[W^{-1}]$, an exact localization functor $Q$, and the characterization of distinguished triangles as triangles isomorphic to images of distinguished triangles. By Step 2 these are precisely images of cone triangles. The chosen larger universe is used for this localization and its morphisms.

For a full additive subcategory $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal C$, its zero object and binary biproducts give $K(\mathcal J)$ the cone triangulation of [lem-trf-additive-homotopy-category-triangulated]; the bounded-below restriction is justified by the bound and subcategory criterion in Step 2 [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. Inclusion preserves homotopies, shifts and biproducts, so sends each cone triangle to its cone triangle (up to the canonical biproduct isomorphism). It therefore carries every triangle isomorphic to one to a distinguished triangle, which is exactness [def-weil-triangulated-category]. All preceding steps also apply when $\mathcal C$ was chosen with fixed bounds $[a,b]$: degree shifts leave filtration indices unchanged, and every cone uses only direct sums with $F^a$ equal to the whole term and $F^{b+1}=0$. No uniform filtration bound over all cochain degrees was used in the unrestricted case.
